apps.title: LAN Scan
apps.summary: Find the devices on your Wi-Fi network and scan their open ports.
apps.description: Lists the devices of the local network with IP, MAC, vendor and name (mDNS, NetBIOS, reverse DNS), then runs a TCP connect scan of the common ports (or 1-1024) on the one you select. Needs no root and no extra tools, and only ever scans the subnet the deck is connected to. Use it on networks you own or are allowed to test.

apps.title: Mesh Hop
apps.summary: Full-screen MeshCore messenger for the deck: chats, contacts, nearby nodes and radio settings on 640x480.
apps.description: A full-screen client for MeshCore LoRa mesh networks. The deck controls a MeshCore companion radio board plugged into its USB port (the radio is on the board, the deck is the screen and keyboard). Two-pane Chats (channels and direct conversations with unread counts, mute and delete options by Ctrl+O or a 3 s hold on the name, search in the whole message archive by words, chat, dates and direction), a Contacts table you can sort and filter by type, time since heard and group, with select mode (bulk delete one by one with a progress box, groups), contact details (key, route, last advert, position) and a Nearby list of the nodes heard (adverts, pending contacts, an active zero-hop scan, Add and Ignore). Settings: board status with its position (a Position box sets it by hand or with the board GPS switch), a statistics screen, a packet log of the radio packets heard (kept in memory only), node name, radio presets (26 built in, refreshed from api.meshcore.nz in the background when the deck is online), bandwidth, spreading factor, coding rate, TX power and the path hash size (1, 2 or 3 bytes) chosen in a popup with arrows, repeat on or off where the board allows it, a scheduled advert, manual add mode and the auto-add types, direct message retries, board clock, board GPS switch, hashtag and private channels, reboot and factory reset of the board (double confirmation), a History section. Your channel messages show "heard back by N repeaters" when they come back from the mesh. Messages, contacts, groups and flags are kept between runs, separately for each board (by its public key), in ~/.local/share/mesh-hop. Text is typed with the Bluetooth keyboard only (there is no on-screen keyboard); touch is for taps, drag-scrolling and buttons, and Tab walks the tabs. Map and Terminal tabs are placeholders for later versions. The board must run the MeshCore companion radio firmware (USB); the user must be in the dialout group. Needs a launcher with full-screen app support (X-Fullscreen in .desktop files).

apps.title: viz1090
apps.summary: Full-screen ADS-B display: live aircraft from an RTL-SDR dongle on a world map.
apps.description: The real viz1090 (by Nathan Matsuda) on the deck, full screen, with its own decoder (readsb with RTL-SDR support), an intro screen (type the nearest airport code, or use a GPS) and a world map. Needs an RTL-SDR dongle with a 1090 MHz antenna and a launcher with full-screen support (X-Fullscreen in .desktop files). Map data: Natural Earth and OurAirports. viz1090: BSD licence; readsb: GPL-3 (source: https://github.com/wiedehopf/readsb).

apps.title: Wi-Fi Survey
apps.summary: See the Wi-Fi networks around you and which channels are crowded.
apps.description: Lists the Wi-Fi networks in range sorted by signal, with SSID, signal strength, channel, band and security, and marks the one the deck is connected to. Tap or press Enter on a network for its details (BSSID, vendor, frequency, rate). A second screen charts the number of networks per channel on 2.4 and 5 GHz and highlights the least crowded channel. Passive only: it reads the scan results of NetworkManager (nmcli), needs no root, and never connects, injects or captures anything.
